info.title: UCP Shopping Service
info.description:
Canonical REST interface for UCP Shopping service. Schema references are logical pointers - actual payload shape is determined by negotiated capabilities.

**Endpoint Resolution:** This spec defines operations only. The base URL MUST be obtained from the merchant's discovery profile at `/.well-known/ucp` under `services["dev.ucp.shopping"][transport=rest].endpoint`. The `{endpoint}` server variable below is a placeholder for tooling compatibility.

put.description: Update Checkout is a full replacement operation. A new Update Checkout operation is not permitted while Checkout status is `complete_in_progress`. Duplicate requests remain subject to Replay Protection. If the Business receives a new Update Checkout request in that state, it leaves the Checkout unchanged and returns the current Checkout with a recoverable error Message.

Actions.title: Actions
Actions.description: Outstanding extension-defined Action instances, keyed by reverse-domain Action type, not extension name.

additionalProperties.description: Non-empty instances of one Action type. JSON preserves array order; the declaring extension defines whether order has processing semantics.

id.description: Adjustment event identifier.

type.description: Type of adjustment (open string). Typically money-related like: refund, return, credit, price_adjustment, dispute, cancellation. Can be any value that makes sense for the merchant's business.

occurred_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp when this adjustment occurred.

id.description: Line item ID reference.

quantity.description: Signed integer count of steps of the referenced line item's `quantity_unit` (`10^-scale` × `unit`); when `quantity_unit` is absent, it counts whole items (`each`). Negative values represent reductions (e.g. returns); positive values represent additions (e.g. exchanges).

measure.description: The settled measurement this adjustment reconciles (for example, actual picked weight), present when the line's price settles by measurement. Its unit identity MUST match the line's pricing basis (`item.unit_price` measure/reference unit); no unit conversion. A pure price settlement uses `quantity: 0` together with `measure` and a totals delta.

line_items.description: Which line items and quantities are affected (optional).

totals.description: Adjustment totals breakdown. Signed values - negative for money returned to buyer (refunds, credits), positive for additional charges (exchanges).

description.description: Human-readable reason or description (e.g., 'Defective item', 'Customer requested').

Adjustment.title: Adjustment
Adjustment.description: Post-order event that exists independently of fulfillment. Typically represents money movements but can be any post-order change. Polymorphic type that can optionally reference line items.

amount.description: Amount allocated to this target in ISO 4217 minor units.

Amenity.title: Amenity
Amenity.description: Buyer-facing presentation metadata for one amenity identifier. The containing map key, not this metadata, defines amenity identity and filter matching.

description.description: Short, plain-text, buyer-facing label or phrase for the amenity, suitable for direct use in a compact list (e.g., 'Curbside pickup'). The Business SHOULD localize it for the request when possible. This content does not participate in amenity identity or filter matching.

AmenityType.title: AmenityType
AmenityType.description: A standardized open reverse-DNS string representing a physical feature, capability, or service provided by a location. Supports a 2-tier hierarchy when defining well-known values in UCP: 1) Common vocabulary for universal features that directly live on `dev.ucp.amenity` (e.g., dev.ucp.amenity.wi_fi) and 2) Industry-scoped features that MUST append their related service name on top of `dev.ucp.amenity` (e.g., dev.ucp.amenity.shopping.in_store_pickup). Businesses MAY define custom vocabulary in their own domain (e.g., com.example.amenity.auto_care_center).

Amount.title: Amount
Amount.description: Monetary amount in the currency's minor unit as defined by ISO 4217. Refer to the currency's exponent to determine minor-to-major ratio (e.g., 2 for USD, 0 for JPY, 3 for KWD).

AppliedDiscount.description: A discount that was successfully applied.

code.description: The discount code. Omitted for automatic discounts.

amount.description: Total discount amount in ISO 4217 minor units.

automatic.description: True if applied automatically by merchant rules (no code required).

method.description: Allocation method. 'each' = applied independently per item. 'across' = split proportionally by value.

priority.description: Stacking order for discount calculation. Lower numbers applied first (1 = first).

provisional.description: True if this discount requires additional verification.

eligibility.description: The eligibility claim accepted by the Business for this discount. Corresponds to a value from context.eligibility. Omitted for code-based and non-eligibility automatic discounts.

Arguments.title: Arguments

conversation.description: Provide a conversation to continue it on a follow-up; omit to start a new one.

ids.description: Optional identifiers that ground the question in any Business resource. A Business SHOULD accept its own Global IDs (GIDs) and MAY accept recognized secondary identifiers such as SKU, handle, or URL. GIDs self-describe to the Business; a Platform may send them as opaque grounding references. Examples include a product, location, cart, order, or booking.

answer.description: Answer provided by the Business. Plain text is required; Markdown and HTML are optional alternative encodings.

html.description: HTML-formatted content. Security: Platforms MUST sanitize before rendering—strip scripts, event handlers, and untrusted elements. Treat all rich text as untrusted input.

answer.title: AskResponseAnswer

conversation.description: Business-issued conversation for multi-turn continuation. When returned, the business SHOULD retain its history until `expires_at` (or per its own policy) so a follow-up with the same `id` builds on it. An unresolved `id` starts a new conversation and is noted in `messages`.

links.description: Optional links and references related to the answer. When a link refers to an addressable UCP resource, the Business SHOULD include its GID in the link's `id`.

messages.description: Errors, warnings, or informational messages about the answer or its grounding.

additionalProperties.description: URL-style parameter value, encoded as a string. Numeric or boolean values MUST be string-encoded as they would be in a URL query string.

available.description: Whether this can be obtained. See status for fulfillment details.

status.description: Qualifies available with fulfillment state. Well-known values: `in_stock`, `backorder`, `preorder`, `out_of_stock`, `discontinued`.

constraints.description: A Constraint Expression describing the instrument this entry makes available. Keys in `properties` name members of the `constraint_target` declared by the instrument schema for this `type`. Requirements on submitted request data belong in `ucp.request_constraints` instead.

AvailablePaymentInstrument.description: An instrument type available from a payment handler with optional constraints.

id.description: Opaque identifier of the bound resource within the owning capability, for example a checkout identifier.

Binding.title: Binding
Binding.description: Binds a credential or token to a specific capability resource. Prevents reuse across different resources.

multi_destination.description: Method types that permit multiple destinations within one cart (e.g. split shipping across addresses). Listing a method permits it; an omitted method does not. Open — businesses MAY list any method type.

method.description: Fulfillment method type (e.g. `shipping`, `pickup`). Optional per-method constraints MAY be added alongside.

method_combinations.description: Method-type combinations the business permits within one cart. Each inner array is a permitted set of method `type` values (e.g. shipping + pickup).

allowed_combinations.description: Array of valid instrument combinations. Each combination is an array of instrument groups. A payment is valid if it matches any combination.

items.description: A single valid combination: an array of instrument groups that together define the constraints. All groups must be satisfied (AND logic).

CardCredential.title: CardCredential
CardCredential.description: Deprecated: use PAN Credential (`pan_credential.json`) or Network Token Credential (`network_token_credential.json`). A card credential containing sensitive payment card details including raw Primary Account Numbers (PANs). This credential type MUST NOT be used for checkout, only with payment handlers that tokenize or encrypt credentials. CRITICAL: Both parties handling CardCredential (sender and receiver) MUST be PCI DSS compliant. Transmission MUST use HTTPS/TLS with strong cipher suites.

type.description: The credential type identifier for card credentials.

card_number_type.description: Deprecated: the credential type now carries this distinction. The type of card number. Network tokens are preferred with fallback to FPAN. See PCI Scope for more details.

expiry_month.description: The month of the card's expiration date (1-12).

expiry_year.description: The year of the card's expiration date.

eci_value.description: Electronic Commerce Indicator / Security Level Indicator provided with network tokens.

CardPaymentInstrument.description: A basic card payment instrument with visible card details. Can be inherited by a handler's instrument schema to define handler-specific display details or more complex credential structures.
CardPaymentInstrument.title: CardPaymentInstrument

id.description: A unique identifier for this instrument instance. Typically assigned by the platform for instruments it collects. For a business-owned saved instrument returned on an identity-linked response, this identifier is assigned by the business; the platform MUST treat it as an opaque, business-scoped reference, and the business resolves it server-side when the buyer selects it.

handler_id.description: The unique identifier for the handler instance that produced this instrument. This corresponds to the 'id' field in the Payment Handler definition.

type.description: Indicates this is a card payment instrument.

billing_address.description: The billing address associated with this payment method.

display.description: Display information for this card payment instrument.

brand.description: The card brand/network shown to the buyer (e.g., visa, mastercard, amex). Presentational only.

last_digits.description: Last 4 digits of the card number.

expiry_month.description: The month of the card's expiration date (1-12).

expiry_year.description: The year of the card's expiration date.

description.description: An optional rich text description of the card to display to the user (e.g., 'Visa ending in 1234, expires 12/2025').

card_art.description: An optional URI to a rich image representing the card (e.g., card art provided by the issuer).

display.title: CardPaymentInstrumentDisplay

amount.description: Contribution amount for this instrument expressed in ISO 4217 minor units of the containing capability object's `currency`. On request: the platform's requested contribution (omit for open-amount). On response: the actual amount authorized or charged (omitted when not finally processed).

network.description: Card network elected for this transaction, typically a co-badged selection. When present, the business MAY decline if the card cannot route over it and MUST NOT substitute another.

CatalogFulfillment.title: CatalogFulfillment
CatalogFulfillment.description: How a catalog variant can be fulfilled. Mirrors checkout `fulfillment`.

CatalogFulfillmentMethod.title: CatalogFulfillmentMethod
CatalogFulfillmentMethod.description: A fulfillment method on a catalog variant: how the variant can be fulfilled, and its availability.

type.description: Fulfillment method type. Well-known values: `shipping`, `pickup`. Businesses MAY use additional values.

description.description: Short buyer-facing summary (e.g. 'Ships in 2–4 business days').

availability.description: Availability of this variant via this method at the specified or inferred location.

location.description: Stable, opaque identifier for the Business Location resolved for this place-based fulfillment method. The Business recognizes the same ID when submitted as `selected_destination_id` for that method; recognition does not reserve inventory or guarantee eligibility, and current terms are revalidated.

options.description: Representative fulfillment options for this method (e.g. Standard, Express). Without a destination or full cart, a Business SHOULD preview meaningful boundary options (e.g. cheapest, fastest); more specific options are negotiated in Checkout once line items and destination are known.

CatalogGetProductRequest.description: Request body for single-product retrieval. Supports interactive variant narrowing via selected and preferences.

id.description: Product or variant identifier. Implementations MUST support product ID and variant ID.

selected.description: Partial or full option selections for interactive variant narrowing. When provided, response option values include availability signals (available, exists) relative to these selections.

preferences.description: Option names in relaxation priority order. When no exact variant matches all selections, the server drops options from the end of this list first. E.g., ['Color', 'Size'] keeps Color and relaxes Size.

filters.description: Filter criteria to narrow returned variants. All specified filters combine with AND logic.

products.description: Products matching the requested identifiers. May contain fewer items if some identifiers not found, or more if identifiers match multiple products.

actions.description: Outstanding extension-defined Actions for this catalog lookup response.

messages.description: Errors, warnings, or informational messages about the requested items.

policies.description: Policies (e.g., return/refund terms) that apply to the products in this response. `applies_to` targets are relative to the response root; when absent or empty, refer to the URLs in `links[]`.

actions.description: Outstanding extension-defined Actions for this catalog search response.

messages.description: Errors, warnings, or informational messages about the search results.

policies.description: Policies (e.g., return/refund terms) that apply to the products in these search results. `applies_to` targets are relative to the response root; when absent or empty, refer to the URLs in `links[]`.

Consent.description: Per-purpose consent. Keys are reverse-DNS purpose identifiers. UCP defines four well-known purposes: `dev.ucp.consent.marketing`, `dev.ucp.consent.analytics`, `dev.ucp.consent.preferences`, `dev.ucp.consent.sale_or_sharing`. Fee.title: Fee
Fee.description: A charge on a return, typed by what it is for, as an estimated maximum. `amount` states a flat charge, where `0` means nothing is charged; `basis_points` states a percentage, optionally capped by `max_amount`; with neither, the fee is charged at its actual cost and no maximum is stated.

type.description: Fee kind, as a reverse-domain name. Well-known values: `dev.ucp.shopping.fee.restocking` (a deduction from the refund, charged per one whole `quantity_unit.unit` returned, for example per lb, or per `each` when `quantity_unit` is absent), `dev.ucp.shopping.fee.return_shipping` (the cost of shipping the return, charged per return shipment), `dev.ucp.shopping.fee.handling` (charged per return request). Vendor kinds use the vendor's own namespace (e.g., `com.example.fee.eco`) and are charged per return request. A vendor fee charged on another basis, such as per item, omits `amount` and states its terms in `display_text`. A fee with an unknown `type` MUST carry `display_text`. Omitted only on an entry with `amount: 0`, which states that the business charges no fee of any kind in its scope, including vendor kinds and kinds defined later.

methods.description: Return channels this fee applies to; omitted means every channel. A channel need not be listed in the policy's `methods`. When more than one entry applies to a fee on a channel, an entry that lists the channel takes precedence over one that does not; among entries that both list the channel or both do not, an entry with a `type` takes precedence over one without.

amount.description: Estimated maximum flat charge, in ISO 4217 minor units of the currency the covered items are priced in, charged per the unit of the fee `type`. `0` states that nothing is charged. Mutually exclusive with `basis_points`.

basis_points.description: Estimated maximum charge in basis points (hundredths of a percent; `1250` = 12.5%) of the amount paid for the returned quantity, after item-level discounts and excluding tax, shipping, and other fees. On catalog surfaces, where no amount has been paid, it applies to the covered product's price. Mutually exclusive with `amount`.

max_amount.description: Cap on a `basis_points` charge: the charge is at most this amount, in ISO 4217 minor units of the currency the covered items are priced in, per the unit of the fee `type`. Requires `basis_points`.

display_text.description: Human-readable fee label, naming any condition under which the fee applies (e.g., '15% restocking fee on opened items'). Required when `type` is not a well-known fee kind, and when the fee has neither `amount` nor `basis_points`.

JwkPublicKey.description: Public JSON Web Key used for HTTP Message Signatures and signed webhook verification. UCP profiles publish public keys only; private key material MUST NOT appear in a profile. Well-known key types: EC (ECDSA P-256, P-384) and OKP (EdDSA Ed25519); OKP keys are RECOMMENDED for signers opting into Web Bot Auth (WBA) interop on HTTP transport. A single profile MAY publish keys of either or both types; consumers select keys by kid. The kty, crv, and alg vocabularies are OPEN: verifiers MUST tolerate key types, curves, and algorithms they do not recognize, selecting keys by kid at verification time. An unsupported key affects only the signature that references it (algorithm_unsupported) and MUST NOT cause whole-profile rejection. Additional public JWK members are permitted; consumers ignore unknown members.

eligibility.description: Structured return eligibility statement. Omitted means eligibility is not stated structurally, not that returns are unlimited or not accepted. When `type` is `not_accepted`, the business's return policy does not accept returns of the covered items, and `supported_resolutions`, `methods`, and `fees` MUST be omitted.

supported_resolutions.description: Return outcomes guaranteed for every eligible return, as an unordered set; not an exhaustive list. Well-known values: `original_payment_method`, `store_credit`, `gift_card`, `exchange`, `replacement`.

methods.description: Return channels guaranteed for every eligible return, as an unordered set; not an exhaustive list. Well-known values: `in_store`, `by_mail`, `kiosk`. Omit when channels are not stated structurally.

fees.description: Estimated maximum charges on a return, each typed by what it is for and optionally scoped to channels; not an exhaustive list. Omitted means fees are not stated structurally, not that none are charged.

ReturnEligibility.title: ReturnEligibility
ReturnEligibility.description: An open return eligibility statement. `window` states a guaranteed minimum period after an anchor event and, once resolved, the instant it ends; expiration does not signal non-returnability. `unlimited` states no time restriction, not unconditional eligibility. `not_accepted` states that the business's return policy does not accept returns of the covered items; it does not describe remedies under applicable law or third-party guarantees. Unknown types establish no eligibility inference; consumers may use the base policy's `description`.

type.description: Eligibility kind. Well-known values: `window`, `unlimited`, `not_accepted`. Unknown values establish no eligibility inference.

duration.description: Length of the return window after the `anchor` event. It states the term for presentation; the Business resolves the deadline as `expires_at`.

anchor.description: Event the window is measured from. Well-known values: `purchased`, `fulfilled`, `delivered`.

expires_at.description: RFC 3339 instant at which the window ends, resolved by the Business once the `anchor` event has occurred (e.g., on an order after delivery). list_price.description: Reference price for comparison display, typically shown as a strikethrough next to `price`, and denominated like `price`. It is not charged and is never part of `totals`; the gap against `price` is a comparison, not a discount. The Business chooses what it is measured against (for example, the price typically charged over a preceding period, or the manufacturer's suggested retail price); what is permitted varies by jurisdiction. `list_price.currency` MUST equal `price.currency`.

unit_price.description: Price per standard unit of measurement, for shelf-style comparison display. MAY be omitted when unit pricing does not apply.

options.description: Option values that define this variant (e.g., Color: Blue, Size: Large).

media.description: Variant media (images, videos, 3D models). First item is the featured media for listings.

tags.description: Variant tags for categorization and search.

metadata.description: Business-defined custom data extending the standard variant model.

seller.description: Optional seller context for this variant.
seller.title: VariantSeller

Variant.title: Variant
Variant.description: A purchasable variant of a product with specific option selections.

VariantPurchaseOptions.title: VariantPurchaseOptions
VariantPurchaseOptions.description: The purchase option fields added to a catalog variant.

purchase_options.description: The ways this variant can be bought, in the Business's order of preference. The first is the default, and the variant's `price` is its `price`. Absent when the variant is bought the ordinary way.

VersionConstraint.description: Version range requirement with minimum and optional maximum.

max.description: Maximum compatible version (inclusive). When absent, no upper bound.

WarningCode.description: Warning code identifying the type of warning. Standard codes are defined in capability specifications (see examples) and have standardized semantics; freeform codes are permitted.
